results.content: Higher gas prices may be among the economic headwinds taking their toll on Republican voters. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment survey found that Republicans’ consumer sentiment fell 9.5 points from July to August. This is one of the biggest monthly drops in the survey’s history, and it outpaced the overall decline in consumer sentiment of 8 percent.

results.content: The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 51.0 in August from 55.2 in July, the first decline in three months and well below the 54.5 consensus forecast. The drop was broad-based, with Republicans showing the steepest decline — sentiment in that group is now 19% below pre-Iran conflict levels and at its lowest since the 2024 election. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.3% from 4.2%, while long-term expectations held at 3.3%.
